3268352:
Zurakan

Zurakan is the walled capital of the nation of Hukaris that sits at the foot of Mount Jabel in the centre of the country.⁠⁠
6904022:
Dome Hive

The Dome Hive is one of the cyclopean monuments of ancient Thassilon, built with the labor of enslaved rune and stone giants.⁠ It is located in the modern Ironbound Archipelago, which was the Thassilonian nation of Edasseril.⁠
12999292:
Itinerant House

The Itinerant House is the only inn in the Widdershins district that allows non-residents to stay overnight. Inside, they can enjoy good food and drink, but being under constant surveillance makes anyone who wants to rest here uneasy.⁠
18617632:
Hapkani

The town of Hapkani was famous for being the location of Hakan Mutalib's Clockwork Vault, situated on a nearby plateau, but after a sandstorm and subsequent desertification of the nearby farmlands have done damage to the city's population. The town is slowly dying, being buried by the sands with fewer and fewer inhabitants each year.⁠
21369942:
Cerulean Spiral

The Cerulean Spiral is a large chasm of nested ruins curled inward like a gigantic nautilus several miles wide and just as deep, located in the Holoma province of Tinhri on the Obari Ocean coast. The area has been the site of many small skirmishes among bands of adventurers fighting for control of and loot in the area, to the point where some believe the area itself drives them to such violence.⁠
24310692:
Latchmin's Folly

Latchmin's Folly is a squat sea fort constructed on a rise in the High Eastwind district of Port Peril.⁠
25162382:
Zetang

Zetang is capital of the empyrean-ruled Tian Xia nation of Tianjing. The Nyenreng Conclave rule from here, many of them too frail to leave the city.⁠ A port city on Point Aykishe along the nation's eastern coast, Zetang was victim of Zo pirate attacks when Lung Wa fell but has since been rebuilt. Rumors suggest the unhappy dead still persist among the shipwrecks in its harbor.⁠
30949792:
Fort Ristin

Fort Ristin marks the easternmost edge of the Chernasardo region. It is one of the oldest structures in the Southern Fangwood and is made of weathered blocks of smooth, gray stone. Chernasardo Rangers have occupied the fort for decades. It provides an excellent staging area against Molthuni forces invading Nirmathas from the south. Its location makes it an ideal base for border patrols. The fort's four stout towers, large keep, and sturdy walls provide a formidable defense. Its architecture is distinctly Chelaxian.⁠⁠⁠

Fort Ristin was constructed by a regional governor named Abdel Ristin during the Everwar.⁠
43824302:
Taranik House

Taranik House is a large mansion in the Rego Scripa section of the Chelaxian city of Westcrown, which serves as the city's garrison for the Hellknight Order of the Rack.⁠
51868052:
Tashagrot

The ruins of Tashagrot are all that remains of the capital of the former Irriseni province of Rimetusk, wiped out by predators coming from the Realm of the Mammoth Lords that were eager to regain their old territories. It is said that the site, which lies on the eastern bank of the Gullik River south of Coldwater, is haunted by its massacred residents.⁠⁠
53008632:
Gold Goblin

The Gold Goblin Gambling Hall is a gaming hall and casino located in the Varisian city of Riddleport. Located in the bustling Wharf District, it hosts a number of games of chance and skill, including bounder, ghoulette, golems, and skiffs.⁠⁠
77917092:
Hatavit

The settlement of Hatavit was a small lumber camp located in Qadira, north of the Southern Tapur Forest. Designed to house slaves who harvest the bounty of the nearby forest, the town was also a post for woodworkers and carvers.⁠

As of 4717 AR, and as early as 4709 AR, various accounts suggested that Hatavit had recently been hit by an unseasonable sandstorm.⁠⁠ This storm either destroyed its watchtowers, allowing its slaves to escape into the forest,⁠ or it had destroyed the camp altogether and forced all of its inhabitants into the northern woods. Rumors also suggested that the sandstorm was a magical event designed to free the camp's slaves.⁠ In any telling, the camp's inhabitants have not been heard from since.⁠⁠

91820442:
Besmara's Boardwalk

Besmara's Boardwalk is located in the eastern part of The Docks, where visitors can participate in carnival games, purchase souvenirs of their visit to the city, or enjoy street food from the various food stalls. One of these stalls features a knife-throwing game with a symbol on the wall of two crossed swords, recognizable as the symbol of the Bladed Bastards, a local Firebrands group.⁠
92394792:
Xin-Grafar

Xin-Grafar, the City of Golden Death, is the lost underground treasure city of Tar-Baphon, the Whispering Tyrant, located on the Isle of Terror.⁠⁠
95762852:
Kelimber's Dry Goods and Supplies

Kelimber's Dry Goods and Supplies is a massive general store in the Redroof district of Kintargo. Kelimber's Dry Goods can provide most of the basic, day-to-day needs of its residents such as food, and even provides a small local postal service. Maercin Kelimber runs the store and is popular with both the locals and the adventuring community, as the store stocks a variety of basic adventuring equipment.⁠ In addition to serving Redroof, Kelimber's also supplies other smaller grocers across Kintargo.⁠
96200802:
Jailed Emergence

The Jailed Emergence is a sinkhole that plummets down into the Darklands, through Nar-Voth and into Sekamina, with a terminus near the drow city of Giratayn. The surface entrance is ringed with stone towers oriented toward defending the surface from subterranean interlopers, and Prophets of Kalistrade fund protective walls that also mask their far quieter slave trade with Darklands drow.⁠
99515582:
Otari

Otari is a small port town near the Immenwood on the south coast of the Isle of Kortos, about halfway between Absalom and Diobel. It is located at the head of a bay of the Inner Sea.⁠ It is a modern but relatively quiet settlement, and is popular among retired Pathfinders, many of whom operate businesses there.⁠ Important to the economy of Absalom as a whole is Otari's lumber trade: timber cut from the Immenwood arrives by road into Otari and, from there, is traded across the Inner Sea region.⁠

120721332:
Gold mine

A gold mine lies about half-way between the northeastern edge of the Narlmarch Woods and the Shrike River to their south,⁠ where a rugged rock formation rises sharply from the hills. A 5-foot-wide fissure at the base of this formation expands into a 20-foot-wide gap, followed by a 30-foot-wide cave leading further below. Gold ore veins dimly sparkle from some of the cave's walls.⁠
130274862:
Halabad

Halabad is a town on the Rampore Isles in the Shackles, inhabited mainly by slaves who are born and raised there. The town is full of ramshackle housing complexes and equally decrepit breeding centers, where slaves are forced to intermingle and create more slaves. Brutal trainers in the town's training camps teach children at an early age to perform the tasks for which they are made for, breaking their backs and spirits.⁠
130584762:
Hocum's Fantasmagorium

The long-shuttered and storied building once known as Hocum's Fantasmagorium, located in the northern end of the Redroof district in the city of Kintargo, Ravounel, was purchased by Maercin Kelimber at some time recent to 4724 AR. Its renovation into a dry goods warehouse has been delayed by infestations of unusual vermin and imps.⁠
130845972:
Yalakheen

Yalakheen is a sacred city of the deity Yahaiya located in the Alavah Desert of Qadira. Its residents are priestesses of the goddess who tend to visitors seeking their prayers to be fulfilled, usually through suicidal sacrifice.⁠
135073312:
Uthong

Uthong (pronounced OO-tong⁠) acts as the de facto military centre of the nation of Tang Mai, despite it officially having no standing army.⁠ The city is located in the mountains in the far east of the country.⁠ Officially, Tang Mai only has a defensive force, though the push to expand them into a full-blown army is growing in popularity as many fear war looming on the horizon.⁠ Tang Mai's military forces based in Uthong afford the city a degree of political influence almost on par with the capital of Surat Prakan, as the five main political factions and their Chaophraya all keep seats within the city.⁠ Uthong is ruled by Chaophraya Patcharin, a deceptive illusionist sorcerer who is known for her isolationist stance and heavily favouring bolstering Tang Mai's defensive forces into a full-blown army. This question of military build-up is becoming a divisive issue, with many questioning the need for a military force in Uthong and Tang Mai in general, particularly given recent abuses of power within the defensive force.⁠
135334442:
Witchbole

The Witchbole is a giant, twisted thorn tree which Treerazer uses as a fortress and palace. As if its appearance were not harrowing enough, the bloated, gnarled tree is completely mobile, crawling slowly through the forest on its writhing roots. The Witchbole's true nature remains a mystery, though the arboreal regents of the Fierani Forest avoid the topic, leading some to believe that the massive demonic arbor was one of their kind before being corrupted to Treerazer's evil will.⁠

The shattered crest of the Witchbole sometimes twists into the outline of a face, although this visage is vague. On its branches are the impaled corpses of those elves who sought to confront Treerazer directly.⁠

In 4725 AR as part of his offensive Treerazer teleported the Witchbole straight to Iadara where he began a ritual to grow in power and destroy the city. Heroes where able to infiltrate the structure and the ripples of magical power within destroyed the tree making it an empty husk now.⁠
140355332:
Kelmarane

Kelmarane is a ruined battle market village in northwestern Katapesh. The village was one of several in the Uwaga Highlands of the Brazen Peaks situated around the battle market. In 4689 AR the Pactmasters abandoned it to ruin. By 4707 AR the Kulldis tribe of kholo had claimed Kelmarane as its own. The village has since become a haven of kholo slavers, human bandits, and disreputable brigands from the northlands.⁠

Aside from the ancient battle market and the ruined church of Sarenrae, most of the structures in Kelmarane are abandoned ruins. Most lack roofs or sturdy walls, but others are solid enough to provide temporary shelter.⁠

The Pactmasters hired Almah Roveshki to reclaim the village.⁠

146010932:
Whitebridge Station

Whitebridge Station was an outpost of the Aspis Consortium on the Vanji River in the Mwangi Expanse. It was located roughly 200 miles upriver from the town of Bloodcove, and was a 200-foot-long fortified wooden bridge across the river with numerous wooden structures built upon it. The Consortium allowed others to use the bridge to cross the river in return for a small toll payment.⁠

The Consortium was breeding the magical fungus known as arcophage here.⁠
146057432:
Harbormaster

In Magnimar, the Harbormaster refers to the building housing the city's harbormaster. As of 4712 AR, the harbormaster was Vert Aigerd, who replaced Odie Phexen by displaying an incredible ability to memorize ship schedules and names.

This three-story stone building is located in the Beacon's Point district.⁠⁠ The distinctive red skiffs of the Harbormaster guides ship traffic through the complexities of Outcast's Cove.⁠
150526572:
Protectorate Anthology

The Protectorate Anthology is where the Learned Guard operates, patrolling the Wise Quarter and they are located on the stairs leading to the Forae Logos which they defend with fervor. While the architecture shares similarities with other buildings on the island, it incorporates elements from civilizations older than Absalom, such as Ninshabur, Vudra, and Thassilon. Each wing of the building serves a specific function, whether as barracks, magical security archives, or surveillance areas. Thanks to its proximity to the Arcanamirium and the College of Mysteries, the guard has more magic at its disposal than other guards in the city and frequently uses magical locks and extradimensional spaces.⁠
161374882:
Longacre Building

The Longacre Building, one of Korvosa's largest buildings,⁠ is home to its feared Arbiters, after whom the building is also known as Arbiter's Hall. It is the site of the city's executions of violent criminals. Neck-snapping hangings take place in the building, located west of City Hall in North Point, while beheadings by axe occur beneath the building in the Deathhead Vault.⁠

Due to the large amount of undead activity in Longacre—second in the city to only the Gray District necropolis—Abadaran and Pharasmin clerics regularly patrol the building.⁠

The building also has a reputation for strange disappearances of prisoners, sometimes for years at a time and often permanently. Those who do return retain only fragmented memories of what happened during their absence; of those who do not, some who work in Longacre insist that some malevolence from below drags prisoners away.⁠
163885382:
Healing Raft

{

The Healing Raft is a boat that clerics from Sarenrae's House of Healing send floating to The Puddles to provide food and healing to its inhabitants. The priests navigate at low tide, inhaling the unbearable smell of those early morning hours, and the people are so desperate that within the first hour of their arrival they have already used up all the resources the raft can provide for that day.⁠
169248032:
Antoll

Antoll is the former capital of Iobaria, serving that role between 3304 AR and the fall of New Iobaria in 4659 AR.⁠
169270712:
Elfmeet

The Elfmeet is a location in Icemark where the Ilverani set up camp whenever they visit the region. They generally travel along a coastal route to avoid the dangers of the inner Stormspear Mountains. Elfmeet features a double ring of standing stones overlooking the sea. The Varki do not treat this site as one of their villages but often visit the location and engage in trade with Ilverani. The Ilverani are fond of Varki scrimshaw, and often trade potent magical items for well-crafted Varki art.⁠
171553502:
Cho-Tzu

Cho-Tzu is the main settlement on the Shenchu Bay island in the Shackles. It is built around a large triangular harbor.

Most of the harbor is used by the Shenchu pirate vessels and the merchants ships. A second city is formed in the remaining part of the harbor consisting of 50 or more junks, rafts, and other ramshackle watercraft occupied by over 200 Tian-Sings, descended from sailors from Zo Piaobo, the floating city of Minata. These folk rarely set foot on dry land and are known to provide services from fortune-telling to midwifery but can also be hired as thugs. Most of the inhabitants of Cho-Tzu are Tian-Sings but the ramshackle neighborhoods on the northernmost side of the city are populated by tengu who escaped from Imperial Lung Wa long ago.⁠
179000962:
Seerspring Garden

The Seerspring Garden is the largest park in Magnimar and forms a tranquil corner of the Keystone district but borders other city districts too. The Seerspring Garden is named after the Seerspring, a beautiful spring that produces pure, crystal-clear water. The spring is said to have been home to a water spirit that acted as an oracle early in the city's history, while this water spirit has long since disappeared it predicted that it would one day return to the Seerspring. This prophecy and the springs generally mysterious nature led the aiuvarin wizard Leis Nivlandis to found the wizard school called the Stone of the Seers directly opposite the Seerspring Garden.⁠

At the center of the spring stands Our Lady of Blessed Waters, a statue that may depict the water spirit. The sculptor is unknown; the statue just appeared in the spring one day shortly after the park's opening.⁠
182497522:
Averaka

The town of Averaka is located on the southeastern coast of the island of Flintyreach in the Linnorm Kingdom of the Ironbound Islands and is predominantly populated by dromaars.⁠
186319992:
Breach Creek Lumber

Breach Creek Lumber is located in Breachill, Isger, near the Crimson Tide Wood where its lumberjacks and carpenters operate. Both a store and a mill, this business is one of the most profitable in town, supplying lumber to many construction projects throughout the region. The forest can be dangerous, so adventurers are often hired to protect the lumberjacks venturing into it. One group within the company is dedicated to acquiring and processing the lumber, led by Narine Howerdell, while the sales team is managed by Xandel Rynearsohn.⁠
196537772:
Myscurial

Myscurial is a small town on Widowmaker Isle in the Shackles. It is built on Sweet Tooth Lake in the island's interior and hosts naval gladiatorial games between captives or poor debtors armed with simple spears in rowboats. The games become more interesting because of the unique beasts brought into the aquatic arena by mayor Salty Chuzek, which include fiendish lukwatas, giant toads, snapping turtles, and an unbeatable, ravenous catoblepas.⁠
197498452:
Kashang

Kashang is a forbidden, ancient ruin of the long-extinct Valashai Empire that is located in the Chenlun Mountains' eastern foothills, in the depths of the deadly Valashmai Jungle. Kashang is a series of many-stepped temples shrouded by the surrounding jungle in utter silence, and no beast from the surrounding jungles dares intrude on Kashang's unholy quiet.

Kashang's buildings are made from dark stone that is eerily clammy to the touch. Whatever horrors the ancient Valashai summoned to aid their long-gone empire still lurks here, waiting for any explorers to upset the delicate magic of the ancient rituals that bind them to the ruins. However, the lore and secrets that lurk within are enough to still draw reckless knowledge seekers to the ruins. Those who seek the foreboding ruins risk paying a terrible price for the forbidden knowledge hidden within silent Kashang.⁠⁠
234941462:
Whitecaps

Whitecaps is one of the oldest inns on the mainland of Korvosa. Located in the North Point district, just south of the Narrows of Saint Alika. Whitecaps feels every bit of its two and a half centuries of age, everything is dated, run down or worn out. Whitecaps does however have an excellent reputation for being clean, cheap and very secure, there have only been 7 burglaries in the last two and a half centuries. However, two of these thefts happened recently and the owner is concerned about Whitecaps losing its sterling reputation for security.⁠
244417852:
Osprey

The Osprey is one of the ten remaining pilings of the Irespan in Magnimar. It is the shortest of the ten, standing only 100 feet high.

There is an entrance into the upper piling. The church of Abadar is rumored to operate a prison here.⁠ Locals believe that political prisoners and others that are best hidden away are held here.⁠

Alabaster Park

Alabaster Park is a small, yet beautiful public park located in the upper-class Alabaster District of the Varisian city of Magnimar.⁠ Found just south of the large hippodrome known as Serpent's Run, the park is popular among citizens of all classes wishing to escape the race day crowds.⁠
298427782:
Jade Circle

The Jade Circle is a teahouse located in the South Shore district that caters to the aristocratic elite of Korvosa. Topped by a huge green dome, the Jade Circle is also graced with an exotic lacquer finish and hung with the banners of various Korvosan noble houses. The Jade Circle is one of the fanciest buildings within South Shore, and during the day it serves fragrant teas from distant Osirion and Tian Xia. At night, the fare changes to upmarket alcoholic beverages, and the clientele, while still elite, becomes noticeably more boisterous.⁠
314305222:
Datorro's Brewery

Datorro's Brewery is an extravagant stall in the Daystalls, the shantytown of vendor stalls, tents, and kiosks in the city of Katapesh. Ano Datorro sells casks, bottles, skins, and mug samplings of his various ales. His workspace is full of still and alchemist's equipment and smokes all day long, churning out a variety of ales.⁠
317477282:
Castle Blakros

Castle Blakros is an imposing black stone structure in the Petal District. The Blakros family lives surrounded by 20-foot-high walls and beautiful gardens near a natural lake. Inside, Lady Hamaria manages the artifacts that don't fit in the Blakros Museum, frequently hiring adventurers to handle problems her own agents can't solve, focusing instead on political and commercial issues.⁠
323220652:
Hazrak

Hazrak is a minotaur settlement located in the Riven Hills of the Isle of Kortos in Absalom. Its inhabitants can trace their town's origins all the way back to the First Siege of Absalom in 23 AR. During this war, the minotaur warlord Voradni Voon brought thousands of his kind through the Brazen Arch to lay siege to Absalom. After their defeat by the god Aroden himself, the surviving minotaurs fled to the central highlands of the island, where they (or their descendants) founded Hazrak, and continue to harass the other races of the island to this day.⁠⁠

Senghor

The port city-state of Senghor is located on the Bay of Senghor, which is part of the Fever Sea on Garund's western coast. It is on the western end of the peninsula known as the Kaava Lands (the kaava are a pygmy tribe of kech) in the southern Mwangi Expanse.⁠⁠
344225782:
Besmara's House

Besmara's House is the temple to Besmara in Ilizmagorti on Mediogalti Island.⁠ It is sited in a converted warehouse in the city's Wharves district. It is the second largest temple in the city: only the Pagoda of the Mantis is larger.

Few of Ilizmagorti's established citizens revere Besmara, but visiting pirates make offerings at the temple before setting out on voyages. The temple's message board is a convenient place for captains to leave their details, in order for potential employers or potential crew to contact them.

The clerics, led by Priest-Captain Ramos Blackarm, seek to cajole or frighten visiting sailors into making a donation to the goddess. They sell "placations" to the gullible, claiming they will protect the bearer from the perils of the sea. They also offer to sell letters of marque and flags of convenience, seeking to increase strife on the high seas in honour of their goddess.⁠

Temple of the Elk

The Temple of the Elk is an overgrown and forgotten shrine to Erastil in the northern Narlmarches. A dense growth of brambles and other thorny plants envelops the expansive clearing where it is situated, deep within the forest.⁠
352376532:
Inspiriting Wellspring

The Inspiriting Wellspring is a remote ruin in the open desert 54 miles from the oasis that serves as a waypoint for travelers between Aspenthar and Pashow in Thuvia; the oasis itself is about 37 miles outside of Aspenthar.⁠
383789292:
Deepmar Penal Colony

Under Chelaxian rule, Deepmar hosted a small penal colony known as Deepmar Penal Colony, where the prisoners mined crystals useful as arcane reagents. The prison camps were abandoned before Ravounel's secession in the Kintargan Rebellion, and the new government has let them remain so.⁠
397979622:
Ayesh

Ayesh is a city on the Alavah Peninsula in Qadira.⁠
403560282:
Sirola Manor

Sirola Manor is a spacious building in Westgate, but not as ostentatious as some others in the city, being the residence of retired Pathfinder Venla and Urmas Sirola.⁠
408424402:
Songbird Hall

Songbird Hall is the temple to Shelyn in the city of Kintargo, Ravounel, and is both the city's third-largest temple and its most trafficked.⁠ Its high priest as of 4724 AR was Zachrin Vhast.⁠
422688932:
Ducotrion

Ducotrion is a single-story stone structure located in the center of the city to respond to any emergency. It also serves as the offices and barracks of the duxotar. Duxotar Ariende Jharnavar is in charge of the guard and is usually in the building.⁠
425573292:
Gulgamodh

Gulgamodh is a gargantuan construct that once stood guard over the Precipice Quarter of Absalom. Passad's Mansion

Passad's Mansion is the magnificent residence of Temel Passad, where he welcomes business partners and agents of the Pathfinder Society to this building overlooking the lake. The other Kalistocrats dislike these dual loyalties, and although they don't act against him directly, they could sabotage his meetings at his home if they so desired.⁠
446041572:
Palette Falls

The Palette Falls waterfall is where the green waters of Emerald Creek and the orange-hued Ironpass River merge before flowing into the Inkwater River. This area, located on the Nesmian Plains in Nirmathas, is the only region that mottled palette berries grow, which can be turned into a unique spice. The unusual water coloring has led to otters with speckled green fur. The pelts of these otters are sold at high prices in Canorate.⁠
450120772:
Lucky Bones

For centuries, Lucky Bones was a notorious gambling house and drug den sat in the heart of Old Kintargo, but it was burned down in a raid by Hellknights of the Order of the Torrent. Unbeknownst to most, Lucky Bones had long served as a legitimate front for the notorious Gray Spiders guild which operated out of the basement below it.⁠
455564642:
Winter Garden

Owned by a former member of the Umbral Court, the Winter Garden is a cottage in the western Uskwood whose land around it is haunted by disorienting mists and unending snowfall.⁠
455733442:
Saffron House

The Saffron House is a crumbling mansion once owned by Cleid Thord located within the murky Sclerain Swamp in eastern Canterwall, one of the counties of Ustalav. There is something very wrong about this haunted and abandoned home: it is claustrophobic inside, the sheet-covered furniture is mouldy and there are noises from within the walls. Many of its room seem stunted or underformed, while others seem cripplingly small. Even stranger is a repulsive yellowing on every surface. Not many know of this house and fewer understand its blighted nature.⁠⁠⁠⁠
484688292:
Gallery Rousa

Gallery Rousa is a popular and controversial art gallery in the Wise Quarter whose exhibitions change regularly and whose subject matter is criticized for its provocative nature.⁠
498804692:
Fort Indros

Fort Indros is located at the north-easternmost point of Magnimar, amongst the riches of the Alabaster District on a spur of land that juts out into the Varisian Gulf. The fort is named after its designer Alcaydian Indros, the founder of Magnimar and a watchful paladin of Aroden.⁠ The fort gives an unmatched view of the surrounding Gulf and serves as a deterrent to any pirates (from Riddleport or anywhere else) who might think of attacking the city. The fort bristles with siege weapons and bowmen. As of 4707 AR, it was overseen by the dwarven commander Vanns Wynmerd.⁠⁠
508688232:
Ravenscry

Ravenscry is a basalt statue in the Atteran Ranches depicting a raven with outstretched wings. It is said that a tribe abandoned the faith of Zon-Kuthon for the spirit faith, and that when the Kuthites learned of this, they sacrificed them on the altar in front of the statue, which they left as a reminder for future generations. The statue has attracted the attention of Adannos Blackraven, patriarch of his tribe, who was seeking ways to protect his son, who was being drawn to a Desnan cult and thus attracting the attention of the Umbral Court. The statue communicated with him, offering advice on how to help his son.⁠

The truth is that the one giving the advice is a vilderavn, who seeks to bring ruin to Adannos's tribe, just as he did in the past with the first tribe he tempted.⁠
514589862:
Freedom Town

Freedom Town is a predominantly human settlement located on the border of the Hold of Belkzen and Lastwall. It is located in fertile farmland due east of the capital of Urgir, north of the Flood Road.⁠
517207292:
Growling Skald

Growling Skald is a mountain ridge of the larger Mindspin Mountains range that contains one of its few volcanically active areas. The low rumble churning underneath is a clear sign of geological activity, though the more poetically minded say that the rumble is a restless giant spirit that haunts the ridge.⁠ The ridge's elevation averages 11,000 feet.⁠
517292632:
Stavintower

Stavintower is a town in eastern Galt, just south of the Boarwood who is quite isolated from the rest of the nation.⁠
534752432:
Drillstones

The Drillstones is one of the many Thassilonian ruins in the wilds of the Linnorm Kingdom of Southmoor. More than three dozen spire-like, 60-foot-tall stone monoliths rise from the northern Kodar Mountains foothills 50 miles southeast of Kopparberget. Each of these monoliths is decorated with strange spiralling gouges, almost as if they were immense drills sent up from underground. Each stone vibrates slightly to the touch, but some nights of the year these vibrations increase into a disturbing buzz. The stones' purpose is unknown, but a mysterious doorway was recently discovered at the base of one of the monoliths that leads to a strange labyrinth, and deactivated clockworks were found inside. Some scholars believe that the Drillstones were the upper edge of a war machine buried underground.⁠
541366032:
Cuttle

Cuttle is a small settlement on the west coast of Mediogalti Island. It is much smaller and less well-known than the island's main settlement of Ilizmagorti.⁠

It consists of a collection of huts on the edge of the beach and serves as a way station for the whalers of the Arcadian Ocean. The whalers pay the Red Mantis for the use of the site, normally in the form of whale oil,⁠ and several of the villagers are Red Mantis members in disguise.⁠⁠ The whalers resupply here and also render the catches.⁠
552402612:
Fort Drelev

Fort Drelev is located on the north-western banks of Lake Hooktongue in the Stolen Lands region of the River Kingdoms and is ruled by Baron Hannis Drelev, originally under a charter from Brevoy.⁠⁠
566866602:
Gilltown

Gilltown is a secluded collection of crude surface buildings in southern Eastgate, a district of Absalom, where azarketi ply their public trades. The surface neighborhood is a facade for an underground and underwater tunnel community leading to the Bay of Kortos. Despite the lack of formal shops, items retrieved by its residents from underwater wreckage can often be bought here, particularly necromantic items.⁠

The azarketi trade on the surface, while underwater they descend to worship their deities and conduct business amongst themselves. The surface is intentionally neglected to keep the existence of the underwater tunnels hidden from humans. Not only pearls, oysters, and marine materials are sold, but the azarketi also recover marine artifacts from past empires, with those from Azlant being the most sought after.⁠
574353022:
Corveilles

Corveilles, sometimes spelled Corveiles,⁠ was a large city in the Thassilonian kingdom of Cyrusian. As of 4707 AR, its location had not been rediscovered.⁠

Fort Ursoss

Fort Ursoss is an abandoned fort on the south bank of the Marideth River in the interior of the Fangwood. The swampy terrain makes travel on foot difficult and serves as a defensive feature. The fort dates back to the Shining Crusade era and was restored by Cheliax after its independence. Nirmathi soldiers burned the fort to prevent it from falling into Molthune's hands, though the stone basement still stands.⁠
640876372:
Creaky Hammock

The Creaky Hammock is a tavern and inn in the Midland district of Korvosa with a distinctly nautical theme. It often serves ships' crews that are ashore for only a few days, as the tavern is so noisy that the only way most customers can get any rest is by drinking themselves to sleep. The Creaky Hammock is run by Destin Smish, who frequently has to deal with drunken sailors passing out on the floor.⁠⁠

Salav

Salav is a Qadiran city located in the Northern Zho Mountains area, sitting at the head waters of the River Ladan in the foothills of the Zho Mountains.⁠ The Northern Zho Mountains region is the poorest of all Qadira's regions and faces the neighbouring land of Taldor just across the Jalrune River, as such it is the least hungry for war with the proud kingdom.⁠
667200982:
Whiterush

Whiterush is a small, isolated village located in the Verduran Forest region of Andoran, along a patch of rapids on the Sellen River. Its inhabitants are known for their friendly, chatty nature, and the town itself boasts cheery-looking houses covered in thatched roofing. The inhabitants of Whiterush are renowned for their distrust of the residents of nearby Rippleden, claiming that Whiterush and its residents are obviously the superior of the two rival villages.⁠
674018102:
Vusker's Carts & Wheels

Vusker's Carts & Wheels is a wainwright business primarily catering to travelers and merchants, located near the north-western edge of town. The business is run by Fadelby Vusker, who inherited it from his parents and has since dedicated himself to repairing the carriages that travel to and from the area. The region is rife with bandits who end up damaging his customers' carts, which only increases his business.⁠
688566882:
Devil's Rest

The Devil's Rest is a centuries-old trading post located on the southern edge of the Sarkoris Scar in Sarkoris. Its name is said to be derived from its purported founder, a Chelaxian noble.⁠
688907472:
Hammer of Knowledge

The Hammer of Knowledge is a blacksmith shop run by one of the finest blacksmiths in the city, Arya Bahrami. He had to leave his home and found a place in Kaer Maga where his skills are highly valued. While the shop creates typical weapons and armor, it also undertakes work on gears and more exotic metalwork.⁠
694139642:
Radya's Hollow

Radya's Hollow is a mining town that was built near mineral deposits in the Hollow Hills, but after a mining accident that killed several people, the mine was closed, and all attempts to reopen it have resulted in further accidents. During the Ironfang Invasion, the town was taken over by hobgoblins who, ignoring the warnings of the locals, reopened the mine, killing several of their own in the process.⁠
703564412:
Lakeside Amphitheater

The Lakeside Amphitheater is the Varisian city of Kaer Maga's best known and most highly respected performance venue. Located in the commercial Downmarket district, this old, open-air stone amphitheater was built on the side of a small hill on the edge of the city's central lake. During the day, anyone can go there for free to see a large variety of entertainers, ranging from jugglers and acrobats to musicians and comedians. At night, the Lakeside Amphitheater hosts spectacular theatrical and musical performances for the city's elite, who pay dearly for the experience of being entertained by torchlight with the lake serving as a constant backdrop.⁠

Merry Widow

The Merry Widow was a ship that was scuttled off the southern coast of Slitherfish Island to the northeast of Mediogalti Island. It is now half beneath the waves; its water-filled lower decks are home to great numbers of sharks and devilfish.

As of 4711 AR the wreck was being used as a temple to the pirate-goddess Besmara, established by a sect known as the Merry Widows. This splinter group is made up of women who have lost their husbands at sea. It is said that some Mediogalti women donate unwanted males to the ship-temple as a sacrifice to the goddess.⁠

Shamara

Shamara is one of the numerous large, prosperous cities that dot the fertile Qadiran region of Pashman. It is located north of the banks of the Pashman River along Pashman's southern border with the neighbouring region of Southern Zho Mountains.⁠⁠
760017802:
Estate of Yargos Gill

The Estate of Yargos Gill is the beautiful residence of one of Absalom's poorest residents, at least in the past, as he had lived in The Puddles but rose to prominence after his insightful contributions during the Black Echelon Uprising. Yargos Gill has attended numerous events with the Pathfinder Society, and no one in the city knows more about military history than he does. He is familiar with all the city's sieges, the history of the Inner Sea wars, and has published several articles specifically on the conflicts in Andoran. The estate's gardens feature many statues of military heroes from the People's Revolt, and he often shares anecdotes with visitors, as he actively participated in the conflict. The three-story stone manor house stands in the center of the garden, topped with a large statue of Talmandor, as the estate has served for decades as the residence of the ambassador of the democratic republic. The third floor is reserved for such visitors, and the first two contain his vast library and museum, which Andoran's allies can view free of charge. However, a fee must be paid if outsiders wish to see it or have him assist them in their research.⁠

Jittery Quill

The Jittery Quill is located in the northeast of the Heights District of Korvosa, between the Jeggare Museum and the University of Korvosa. It serves both ale and coffee and is open for 24 hours a day for six days. Every Oathday it closes at noon, reopening at dusk the next day. The Jittery Quill is most popular with members of the University, and many study there at all hours.⁠⁠⁠

766331392:
Spire of Lemriss

The Spire of Lemriss, also called the Green Spire of Lemriss,⁠ is a tree-like growth hundreds of feet in height located in western Varisia on the border between the Fogscar Mountains and the Churlwood. Its core is composed of braided and twisted wooden trunks, surrounded by arm-deep shell of vines. Countless birds and forest creatures make their home within its near-vertical structure, their chirps and hoots heard for miles around. Some believe that the spire is a cutting from the World Tree, although this has never been proven.⁠⁠

Nestled in Katapesh's Inner City district, the Grand Coliseum is one of Golarion's largest arenas, capable of comfortably housing 10,000 spectators. The arena is home to many forms of entertainment, from parades to gladiatorial bouts, but by far the most popular is a ball game called ruk.⁠

Many of Katapesh's guilds field, fund, and promote highly competitive ruk teams, and many former players return to the Coliseum to sell their services as trainers and coaches.⁠

Concurrent Currency is a currency exchange business run by the charismatic Darelli Gammathumalshire and the affable Bagwell Thomkin in The Docks district. Logas is the second city of the nation of Isger. It was once the capital until that honor passed to Elidir, and its nobility dream of restoring Logas to its rightful status as the country's first city.⁠

Aphet Mines

The Aphet Mines are three interconnected copper mines in the Footprints of Rovagug. They are some of the few existing mines that have not been completely depleted by the Pharaohs' demands for weapons and ornamentation.

The mines are owned by the Aspis Consortium and overseen by Falsin Deek. Under the operation of Deek, the mines produce consistently high output, and also operate as a front for the Consortium's movement of goods and people into and out of Osirion.⁠

The nearby town of Aphet East provides support to the mine's workers.⁠
823367342:
Encarthan Coast

The Encarthan Coast is the stretch of coastline on the eastern side of Nirmathas that provides access to Lake Encarthan and includes the river deltas of both the Marideth River and the Tourondel River. Of all the nations bordering the lake, Nirmathas has the least-developed coastline, consisting of swamps where only fishing boats can navigate. Alder, gum, and willow trees cover the area, and the only large settlement in the region is Tamran, the capital. Fort Faelon is the second-largest, but is not much more than an inhabited ruin. Due to the war with Molthune and its maritime blockade, few exports pass through the area, leaving it isolated from other neighboring countries.⁠

839225352:
St. Caspieran's Salvation

St. Caspieran's Salvation, also called St. Caspieran's Mission, is an almshouse and temple of Sarenrae founded decades prior to 4708 AR by St. Caspieran, an idealistic Sarenite priest and missionary who comforted the unfortunate, drunk, and orphaned.⁠⁠

Wyo's Rest

Wyo's Rest is a small Qadiran island located off the Alavah Peninsula, nestled in the waters between Sedeq and the Meraz Desert.⁠

Wyo's Rest is named after Lady Wyo, a powerful siren who rules the island. Lady Wyo is accompanied by a harem of male suitors provided by the city of Sedeq who all spend four years living a life of indentured luxury. In exchange, Lady Wyo guards the island and allows Qadiran ships to pass, even helping any vessels in distress.⁠

The island is covered in both verdant plant life and elaborately designed architecture.⁠

Bovodport

Bovodport is a dwarven city in the nation of Zavaten Gura on the coast of Cholpod Gulf.⁠ It is Zavaten Gura's primary center of trade and commerce.⁠
849103432:
Bookmaker

Bookmaker is the largest bookshop in all Korvosa and it attracts eager readers from across the city. Owned by the aiuvarin Costa Serimus, the books on offer within Bookmaker range from books of legends about Ancient Azlant to up-to-date academic reports on Osirion archaeology. Students from Theumanexus College, the University of Korvosa, and various other smaller schools and colleges all buy their books from Bookmaker and many of the professors of these institutions have their published works available in the store. Notably, the students of the Acadamae do not purchase their books here. Bookmaker has an informal agreement to avoid too much overlap with the bookshop Gilded Orrery: the Gilded Orrery focuses on all things arcane, while Bookmaker instead stocks titles with a more general focus on knowledge. Bookmaker sits above a hidden entrance to the maze of underground chambers known as The Vaults.⁠

Silken Court

The Silken Court is a brothel in the Petal District of Absalom. It is the city's most expensive establishment of its type, and among of the Inner Sea's most famous. Previously owned and managed by Elissa the Fair⁠ until her recent retirement, it has since been fully renovated by its new manager, the Calistrian Head Hetaera Dyrianna of House Avenstar.⁠
856368962:
Thorn River bandit camp

The semi-permanent hideout, known as the Thorn River bandit camp lies roughly 60 feet from the Thorn River in the Narlmarches. It is set up on both sides of a narrow, meandering creek and a forest trail that runs beside it. The camp is inhabited by eleven bandits, who are responsible for raiding Oleg's Trading Post in the name of the Stag Lord.⁠

Omash

Omash is a fortress-city in northern Qadira near the border of Taldor that lies on the eastern end of the Satrapy's patrols.⁠⁠ The city contains a dozen schools of war from which the satrap personally chooses warriors for special duties. Each of them specializes in a different tactic or troop type: there are schools for horse cavalry, camel cavalry, carpet cavalry, archery, polearms, siege warfare, and castle-storming. Some of the Peerless, the personal advisors to the satrap, have come from these schools.⁠⁠

Metro-Cathedral

The Metro-Cathedral is a church in Abadar, The Puddles, where the organ, which survived the earthquake of 4698 AR, is played every Oathday. The cathedral is currently without a congregation, although a priest occasionally visits to inspect the structure.⁠

935092072:
Ten Thousand Summer Palace

In the time of Imperial Lung Wa, the Ten Thousand Summer Palace in southern Bachuan, on the northern eaves of the Chang Liao Jungle,⁠ was a favorite winter retreat for many emperors. The palace was an enormous walled compound tended by a vast staff of sorcerers and clerics. During the Bachuan Revolution, the palace was besieged by the revolutionary armies, but its spellcasting inhabitants shut its gates and blasted the rebellious peasants to ash. The palace's gates never opened again.⁠

Although the revolution succeeded in taking over Bachuan, no infiltrators have entered the Ten Thousand Summer Palace and returned to tell the tale, with one single exception. A mercenary from Minkai emerged, covered in glowing sigils and clutching a gigantic emerald, only to die as he stumbled into a nearby village muttering the words, "...beautiuful...terrible..."⁠

In 4724 AR Hao Jin and five of her companions were able to enter after offering bronze statuettes representing the signs of the zodiac. Inside, people in white robes with runes led them to meet someone, and two hours later they emerged. Rumors began to circulate that a direct heir to the throne of Lung Wa was inside, having prolonged his life by entering stasis for almost a year, only emerging one day at a time. As an heir of Lung Wa, he knows the true name of each zodiac beast, and those who can bring other statuettes can receive answers to their most intimate questions.⁠

Isle of Arenway

The Isle of Arenway is located at the confluence of the Verduran Fork and Sellen River in central Taldor. Set in the heart of the Verduran Forest, it is the headquarters of the local druids of the Wildwood Lodge.⁠⁠ It is said to contain a series of standing stones which create an annual connection to the demiplane known as the Circle Between every solstice.⁠

In their summer solstice Moot of Ages, the Green Faith druids from all over Golarion gather in the Isle of Arenway to bring their discoveries before the entire druid community.⁠

The Isle also contains an unnamed harbour outpost of the Taldan River Guard, although by the Treaty of the Wildwood, its sailors are forbidden to leave their walled compound, except to patrol the Sellen River and Verduran Fork. Ships traveling past often stop at the outpost to have their vessels blessed by the druids.⁠

Broken Bridge

Broken Bridge is a massive ruined causeway that once crossed its namesake Brokenbridge River. Located halfway between the city of Yanmass and the start of the Verduran Fork, it was destroyed by a silver dragon sometime during the Dragon Plague between 3660 and 3672 AR. Rather than rebuild the bridge, locals left it as a memorial to the destruction and horrors of dragonkind's decade-long rampage across the country. The open-air plaza features sheets of marble stone hundreds of yards long that bear tile-mosaic depictions of dwarven life within the Darklands before the start of their Quest for Sky. Scenes include battles against ropers, cave worms, and orcs.

The plaza's artworks are among the only untouched and preserved remnants of Koldukar to survive in Urgir. Many have been defaced or destroyed by orcs or earthquakes since Koldukar was conquered in -3708 AR.⁠⁠

996413492:
Jundlan Wrecks

The pirate lords of Issia (now part of Brevoy) once engaged one another in a massive naval battle on the Lake of Mists and Veils. During the battle, the fleets were caught up in a massive storm and wrecked off the coast of Brevoy in Jellicoe Bay. The wreckage remains there to this day, and is known as the Jundlan Wrecks. Presumably a considerable amount of pirate treasure can be found amongst the frost-covered tangle of wrecked ships and ancient, waterlogged corpses. However, numerous unfriendly fey now live amongst the destruction, building altars and structures made from the dead pirates' treasure. On moonless nights at midnight, ghostly bells toll here and gangplanks made of bone extend from the shipwrecks and invite all to board.⁠⁠

Mystic's Redoubt

Mystic's Redoubt is the only public arcane library in Port Peril. It is a six-winged circular tower in Crescent Harbor, and it charges fees of as much as 1,000 gold pieces per year for its use. A small number of apprentices join the library each year, while other scholars visit Mystic's Redoubt to study relics in its antiquities hall. Rare natural components also grow in an adjacent, well-maintained garden.⁠

Shepherd's Rock

The cliff-top citadel of Shepherd's Rock is situated in the Napsune Mountains in Rahadoum and has a commanding view of the nearby desert. As of 4711 AR, it was the centre of operations for the Pure Legion and residence of the organisation's leader Karsakim, the Sword of Man.

The citadel's Vault of Lies houses the Legion's vast store of confiscated religious writings.⁠ It also trains new recruits into the Pure Legion.⁠
1016702312:
Creeping Watcher

The Creeping Watcher is a 70-foot-tall statue in the heart of the Vargas Swamp.

Though draped in vines and surrounded by dense trees, the Creeping Watcher resembles its sister statue, the Crouching Jackal. its body is sleek and cat-like, though covered in carved scales while its head is clearly reptilian. Unlike the Crouching Jackal, the Creeping Watcher is not carved from a single solid lump of stone, and its eyes are made of some sort of luminous yellow stone. Like its sister statue, the Creeping Watcher's origins are surrounded by mystery, though it is generally held that the Creeping Watcher is the more sinister of the two. Some even suppose that the Crouching Jackal serves as some sort of guardian keeping the Creeping Watcher in check. Whatever the truth is, the location has a bad reputation nowadays as it is believed to be the site of foul worship and evil rituals.⁠

Corpselight

Corpselight is a small farming settlement in the undead nation of Geb situated north of the Axan Wood and about two day's travel east of Graydirge.⁠

Sirathu

Sirathu has long been overlooked by its ruling city of Korvosa, holding the undesirable honor of being both the poorest and farthest removed of the city-state's holdings. It was a relatively late addition to Korvosa's realm, ceded from Kaer Maga in the Treaty of Sirathu in 4663 AR.⁠

The town is constantly reminded of their leaders' disregard for them by the White Prince's Fountain which sits in the town square. While the fountain was being constructed, nobles in Korvosa promised that it would be enchanted to provide a clean and endless supply of water for the town, so they would never be dependent on wells. The fall of the Chelaxian Empire diverted the Korvosans' attention, and the well was sadly never completed.

In 4707 AR a local girl was found unconscious on the edge of the fountain, which was miraculously flowing for the first time. Since then, this young girl, blessed by Pharasma, has been a galvanizing force in a growing unrest among the citizens of Sirathu, prophesying that change was coming and that the town should break free of Korvosan control.⁠⁠

Drezen

Iarna

There are three resorts catering to the aristocracy as well as expensive restaurants and two grand theaters.⁠

The hot springs began bubbling up some 200 years ago and are thought to have magical and medicinal powers although nothing has been proven. Hundreds of ageing or sick Jadwiga bathe in the hot springs every year. The truth is that a trapped and insane magma elemental heats Iarna's springs. The elemental was summoned by druids of the Heralds of Summer's Return 200 years ago but was captured and bound by Iarna's baroness at the time. As of 4713 AR, the ruler of Iarna was Baroness Iracetta, who knew the truth but preferred not to damage the town's businesses. Jazdya Vacalav, captain of Iarna's town guard, often fights fire and magma scamps who are attracted by the insane elemental.⁠

It can be accessed only during low tide, as there are jagged rocks and supposedly sea monsters that feed on the prison's dead. Potential invaders must climb wet, sharp stone stairs that wind up the outside of the island and overlook cliffs of the same jagged rocks that are under the waters. This is the only path up the island and is riddled with locations perfect for ambushes or hidden guard posts.⁠

The prison part of the citadel is said to delve not only into the earth but also under the waves of the ocean surrounding the island. The lowest levels have special cells for more powerful prisoners that have been developed over many decades, and might house powerful creatures that must be caged as well as imprisoned.⁠ Some have unusual layouts, such as aquatic terrariums or enchanted game boards. Various lake plants found on Lake Tapipallati, which surrounds the island Talípas is built on, can be crushed into a paste that is then fermented for several weeks. The drink created from this fermentation, also called "talípas", is highly intoxicating. 1320891952:
Kavapesta

Kavapesta is the population center for the Ustalavic county of Amaans, located on the shores of Lake Kavapesta.⁠

The largest city in Amaans and a holy city for Pharasmins, Kavapesta is a somber place possessed by a dour variety of religious fanaticism. The city takes its name from Mother Kavapesta, a Pharasmin missionary and teacher whose sermons on perseverance and suffering laid the foundations for the philosophies today known as the Pharasmin Penitence. After the priestess's death, her followers began the construction of Cryptgate Cathedral, which through centuries of renovations and expansions would become the largest church and monastery of Pharasma in Ustalav. The effort of constructing this monument and the tombs beneath brought droves of pilgrims to the banks of Lake Divirmis, which the faithful eventually renamed Lake Kavapesta. With the cathedral's completion, the assembled congregation lingered on, hoping to create a community based on the tenets of their faith. This community grew slowly, finally becoming the city known today.

Yet a city needs more than faith to survive, a fact the people of Kavapesta stubbornly defy. The foothills around the city are poorly suited to farming and the lake is tainted by poisonous minerals from the Hungry Mountains. A few mines in the surrounding hills scrape tin and coal out of the earth, though one has to wonder if the coin won from these efforts is worth the lives lost to cave-ins, choking maladies, and more mysterious disappearances. But worst of all are the plagues, the rampant sicknesses that seem to boil up from Lake Kavapesta once a generation and burn through the city like a field fire. Scourges like the Whithers, Tol's Voice, and, most fearfully, the Bleak Breath have killed thousands in their beds, with lesser scares and re-emergences occurring every few years. But the people claim that their city is blessed—not cursed like so many visitors say—insisting that each new calamity is a test from Pharasma and an opportunity for the citizens to experience ever greater trials, assuring greater rewards after death.

Field of Bones and Black Glass

Wandering Spheres

The Wandering Spheres is a massive ruined orrery located in central Kyonin with human-sized planetary spheres that once must have risen above the treetops. 1520685802:
Rose and Rake Theater

The Rose and Rake Theater, sometimes spelt the Rose and Rake Theatre, is the beating heart of the Ordellia district of the Varisian city of Magnimar. Ordellia has always regarded itself as somewhat of a separate political entity from the rest of the city being separated from them by the Yondabakari River. The Rose and Rake Theater, an open-air theatre that is renowned for its scathing political satires and controversial critiques of Magnimar's government, serves as the heart of this political entity.⁠
1525872342:
Dacilane Manor

The Dacilane Manor is an impressive four-story structure in the Ivy District surrounded by magnificent gardens, where Lady Miranda Dacilane resides. The house is decorated with chelaxian and asmodean ornamentation.⁠
1529909152:
Gottacker

Gottacker is a small community located on one of the tributaries of the Profit's Flow, inhabited by exiles from the Five Kings Mountains. The settlement is therefore a pleasant destination for those seeking to rewrite their past after making mistakes from which there is no return.⁠
1530937952:
Mercy

Delmon's Glen

Delmon's Glen is a small gnome town located in the far east of the Grungir Forest, in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings, at the point where the Summermelt River flows into the Thundering River; the town's current mayor is Bavakanka Winterlisp.⁠⁠

Delmon's Glen is located along the most important overland trade route that connects Jol and Varisia to the south with the northern lands. The town is unusually mundane for a gnome settlement. Most of its buildings are like Ulfen buildings except for their small size. A few larger buildings catering to visitors are located on the edge of the town, like a trading post and the popular Raven's Best inn.⁠

The small town has had trouble in the past with monsters from the southeastern badlands, especially bulettes, and Bavakanka Winterlisp many times recruited visiting adventures to protect her town.⁠
1563021132:
Ulduvai

Ulduvai was the last of the Shory flying cities in Garund and the Inner Sea region. In a misguided effort to restore the Shory Empire, the sorcerers of Ulduvai consorted with the powers of the Dark Tapestry, which ended up with the entire population being driven mad by a shoggoth servant of Azathoth. The city crashed upon Mirrshock Glacier in the southeastern Mwangi Expanse, south of Mount Dowama in the Shattered Range in -507 AR.⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠

Three ancient Shory sorcerers survived to the present, albeit as undead creatures: Yakmar, the insane adventurer-mage; Yithdul, the arcane diplomat; and Banderak, former head of the city's aeromantic corps.⁠
1567315302:
Three Rings Tavern

The Three Rings Tavern is a tavern in the Five Corners district of Korvosa that belongs to a retired Pathfinder named Theandra Darklight. Theandra is a good-natured bartender and is always hungry for any tales of adventure or daring-do. The Three Rings Tavern is comparatively quiet, serving as much coffee as it does alcoholic beverages. The Three Ring's bouncer Tauk Par keeps a close eye on things and barely manages to conceal his dislike for all of the taverns clientele. As well as a wide range of drinks, the Three Rings Tavern is renowned for its breakfast services which include local staples like Varisian sweetbreads all the way to exotic pastries whose recipes come from distant Geb.⁠
1571311332:
Port Freedom

Situated on the northern bank of the Korir River delta, Port Freedom is Vidrian's second port, behind the capital Anthusis.

The sandbanks of the delta mean the port cannot accommodate large, deep-water ships and are also a serious hazard to the river trade with Kalabuto. Barges travelling the river normally call upon the services of the Rivermen's Guild, native Mwangi pilots who are the only people skilled enough to reliably navigate the river.⁠⁠
1577503362:
Merotsi Mines

The Merotsi Mines are a series of abandoned mines in the Footprints of Rovagug that contained a Rovagug spawn born in a pool of acid. Located about 30 miles from Tar Kuata, the miners abandoned the area after striking a thermal zone that filled the mine with toxic gases, and it was abandoned over a century ago.⁠ In 4715 AR, a Rovagug cult led by Tasutek took over the mines to use as a temple, until the Pathfinder Society sent agents to rescue their victims and destroy them.⁠
1583452712:
Wondervale

The Wondervale was created decades after Aroden's death by Absalom's intellectuals, who sought to showcase the city's inventions and demonstrate that it had not declined in relevance after the death of its patron god. They chose Eastgate and Green Ridge as the venue for they were the least populated areas with the largest open spaces, and proceeded to construct illuminated bridges, Tian Xia-style towers, Vudra pagodas, and Casmaron palaces. The resulting intellectual and cultural exchange was a resounding success, drawing attention to the nation. After the festival, the structure was abandoned, and the escaped plants and animals give the site a sense of ancient ruin, a place favored by lovers, poets, and followers of Brigh. The most striking features are the Jalmeray-style flying towers, teeming with bats.⁠
1597929852:
Shucked Oyster

The Shucked Oyster is a brothel in the Dockway district of Magnimar. Seeshaw Raccas is its madam.⁠

Helsingbyen

Galizhur

Seredain

Penitents

The Penitents are a group of 18 religious pilgrims who as of 4712 AR had been stranded on the island of Hesmene's Grotto in the Shackles. They are led by the paladin Jayhalle Messierre, and include worshipers of both Erastil and Abadar. Messierre does his best to keep the arguments and petulant bickering between the members of the Penitents to a minimum, all the while fending off the unusual and deadly creatures found on the island. They occasionally come into conflict with the Merry Pranksters, a group of pirates who are also stranded on the island, and even more rarely join forces with the buccaneers to fight against their common foe, the rusalka Blue Hesmene.⁠
1642258112:
Sleeping Dove

The Sleeping Dove is a shrine dedicated to Sarenrae located in the western reaches of central Katapesh, less than 100 miles east of Solku.

The history of Sleeping Dove is not a happy one: over 100 years ago, a group of pilgrims dedicated to Sarenrae were on a pilgrimage to Solku when they were ambushed by monstrous bandits—some say kholo, while others say jackalweres—and were slaughtered. A week later the bodies were found by passing travellers, who saw their tattered white gowns blowing in the wind and thought they looked like doves.

Several paladins from Solku came out to the site and built a shrine to Sarenrae here to remember their fallen brethren. Ever since the shrine of Sleeping Dove has been sacred ground. Many a traveller stops to rest by the shrine as it seems to repel evil creatures and has even granted mysterious, and sometimes prophetic, dreams to good and devout creatures.⁠
1642891542:
House of Seven Faces

The House of Seven Faces is a Westgate temple dedicated to Desna where her followers can rest. The clergy dislike ostentatious cathedrals, so there is little decoration except for the seven faces that appeared on the facade the first night the temple was built, and whose origin remains a mystery. There are many theories: some link the seven faces to Thassilon, others suggest they represent Sivanah and that Desna and she are the same person—a theory met with laughter or annoyance by the clergy. But the most sensible theory points to a connection with the Sevenfold Cynosure, where she dwells, the realm being a tribute to the seven planets Rovagug destroyed first. The faces, then, represent seven cultures from these planets that may have arisen and they also serve as a memorial.⁠

Beehive

Deep within the Barrier Wall mountains of Katapesh, a network of chambers joined by winding tunnels forms a well-protected complex. Known as the Beehive, it is located on the southern road to Nex and has a number of widely known entrances.

Inhabitants have included smugglers, slavers, bandits, kholo, dwarves, and bee-like thriae, from which the tunnels got their name. Currently, a hive of formians inhabits the Beehive, though they mostly toil digging new tunnels underground and rarely interact with the surface.⁠
1693198982:
Greenstar Market

The Greenstar Market is an open-air market showcasing typical foods from the Lirgen and Yamasa populations, including live fish brought in barrels, and attracting a large local lizardfolk population. Most of the vendors are Yamasan who brought their farming techniques and products, while the buyers are Lirgeni who, by having similar cultural practices to the Absalomians, were able to keep more wealth. There is a cultural divide: the Lirgeni want to preserve these foods as part of their culture, whereas in the past, the same foods were considered appropriate only for the Yamasan who were considered backwaters. These, in turn, are unsure whether to adopt the food they had to subsist on during their impoverished refuge as a cultural symbol or not.⁠
1697437622:
Eagle's Head

Eagle's Head is both an amphitheatre and the settlement that assembles around it every summer while the theatre is in season. Located in the Kazuhn Prefecture of Taldor, Eagle's Head has existed for many millennia, having been built shortly after the god Aroden ascended to full godhood at the beginning of the Age of Enthronement. Ever since then, Eagle's Head has been a centre for the performing arts which attracts viewers and performers from across the Inner Sea region. Practically, every major work of Taldan drama has been performed at Eagle's Head. Every performer from across Taldor dreams of performing here and that their performance captures the imagination of the people and elevates them as a new cultural phenomena, as has happened to countless artists before them.⁠⁠

Every summer, the land for a mile around Eagle's Head becomes a makeshift city of tents, performers, and theatre-goers that is in constant flux as artists and theatre aficionados come and go as the season progresses. This chaotic atmosphere also proves a heaven for those with less-refined interests. Scheming nobles, spies, revolutionaries, and just plain old criminals all use the cover of the Eagle's Head season to conduct their business, its underhanded side an open secret across the nation. The Brotherhood of Silence, one of the Inner Sea's largest thieves' guilds, has a large presence at Eagle's Head. Many members of the Brotherhood of Silence use Eagle's Head as a place to lie low after committing particularly attention-grabbing crimes in nearby Oppara. Eagle's Head propmaster Rouriss Barthel is secretly a member of the Brotherhood and is the closest thing it has to a leader in the theatrical city.⁠⁠

Because of the amount of espionage, intrigue, and general skulduggery that goes on at Eagle's Head, the Lion Blades, Taldor's secret spy organisation, has a strong presence here. They are led by Myro Gravilla, a long-time regular of Eagle's Head, and between them they attempt to keep a secret catalogue of all the season's intrigues. Unbeknownst to most, almost every season sees the Lion Blades foil some major plot to disrupt, poison, invade, or destroy Eagle's Head. The Lions Blades keep this undercover, this way next season's villain will assume the festive settlement to be an easy target.⁠⁠

For the last five years, the elven virtuoso Tirilee Ambrasa has been the talk of Eagle's Head. This is a near-unprecedented hot streak, most performers are only able to claim the spotlight for, at most, a couple of seasons. Despite being a powerful bard, Tirilee's popularity seems to have nothing to do with magic. Her sway over the attendees gives Tirilee incredible access to the Taldan nobility and prestigious guests from other nations meaning the Lion Blades keep a close eye on her. Tirilee maintains an air of mystery by returning to her home nation of Kyonin at the end of every season.⁠⁠

Jade Monkey

The Jade Monkey is a tavern in Alcasar run by two brothers, and it's well-known among the city's alchemists as a meeting place to discuss their formulas.⁠
1707640262:
Shrine of Sarenrae

An abandoned shrine to the goddess Sarenrae exists in the Underbridge district of the Varisian city of Magnimar. It was built in the early days of the settlement by a priest of the goddess named Father Vosten, who felt that the burgeoning community could use the Dawnflower's guidance.

He was approached a few months after its completion by Sczarni thugs who demanded protection money. When he refused to pay and attempted to drive them off, he and his acolytes were killed. Their bodies were buried in the small graveyard behind the shrine.

The shrine has lain abandoned ever since, as no devotee of Sarenrae has come forward to rebuild it.⁠⁠
1713845522:
Vizio's Tavern

Vizio's Tavern is an establishment in Rego Scripa whose former owners left for Corentyn after the death of a family member, leaving the tavern empty. It was bought by a couple who used it for their confidential meetings to plan acts of rebellion.⁠
1713883962:
Tower of the Ironwood Watch

The Tower of the Ironwood Watch was a beautiful fortress of magical crystal erected by the elves of the Mierani Forest on the border with their neighbors in the kingdom of Cyrusian. The tower received guests of all kinds and was filled with luxuries for these diplomatic delegations. Ten millennia have left only the lower levels of the tower intact, and from the outside it appears as a curiously shaped hill in the treeless Velashu Uplands, as the forest receded until the area became grasslands.⁠ Drow of the House Vexidyre began to live in the structure after being driven from Celwynvian by the return of the elves, and Inexora Vexidyre, a follower of Shax, began raiding the surface for resources while they searched for a way to return home.⁠ In 4713 AR, a group of pathfinders discovered the location and defeated the drow cabal living within.⁠
1720479262:
Little Oppara

Little Oppara is the only settlement on the Taldas Isle in the Shackles. The little town was a small pirate haven but, in 4656 AR, Danziul Maxeme took control of the island and remade the town to mirror the opulence of far-off Taldor. Little Oppara's fine taverns serve delicacies from across Golarion, and richly attired men and women frequent plays and operas at the famed Blooming Rose Theater.⁠
1725711082:
New Anglemire

The original town of Anglemire was a coastal town in Cheliax and stronghold of House Davian until their defeat during the Chelaxian Civil War.⁠ House Thrune, who had defeated House Davian's forces at the nearby city of Corentyn in the Battle of a Hundred Kings in 4639 AR, then starved House Davian's nobles to death in a year-long siege of the town's keep of Emberhold, torched the keep, and withdrew all support for the town. Its surviving residents persisted until orcs, trolls, and other dangers drove them away, leaving the town an abandoned ruin of stone structures.⁠

The children were finally freed, when their dead parents arose from their tilled graves and murdered Cormegi and his men. The place is now staunchly avoided by the swampers of the region.⁠⁠

Temple of Sarenrae

A marble Temple of Sarenrae stands atop Korvosa's Citadel Hill. The opulent structure is considered Korvosa's most expensive building per square foot.⁠⁠

Szamrak's Haven is a hidden enclave of androids, and the largest settlement of androids, in Numeria.⁠
1930486102:
Pridon's Hearth

Pridon's Hearth marked the most southerly point of expansion of the historical Chelaxian colony of Sargava,⁠ now known as the independent nation of Vidrian.
1943277942:
Mama Shrog's Solutions

Mama Shrog's Solutions is a shop that was bought years ago by a woman called Mama Shrog. The building has a grotesque history, having belonged to a painter who murdered his entire family to obtain the specific colour of red he sought. Mama Shrog is a curious old woman who claims to be able to answer her visitors' questions, and although she has no children, she calls everyone her own.⁠ The shop primarily sells alchemical products to address her customers' physical ailments, and although people view Shrog with suspicion because she doesn't hide her faith in Lamashtu, there is no evidence that she has committed any crimes. Several champions and holy warriors have tried to expel her from the city and close the shop, but they haven't made any progress through legal means. When some Firebrands have tried to forcibly remove her, demons appear to defend her with extreme violence, which she justifies as self-defense when questioned by the guards. Although the shop is the only obvious temple of the goddess, shrines are also springing up throughout the city, taking advantage of Absalom's religious freedom.⁠
1947421682:
Common House

The Common House is the Freemen's base of operations, where they meet to discuss plans for the liberation of slaves and other matters. The building also serves as the temple of Cayden Cailean, who invites clerics to cast their magic in exchange for free drinks and lodging. In times of crisis, the house springs into action, and an internal militia prepares to protect the freedoms of its people against their former masters.⁠
1948586502:
Ahkmed's Carpets

Ahkmed's Carpets is a shop in the Lower City's bazaar of the city of Katapesh. The rugs and tapestries of the shop are famous all over the world. The area of the shop is a maze of hanging rugs, tapestries, sleeping pallets, and other woven creations. The owner of the shop, Ahkmed is a high-ranking member of Katapesh's Guild of Weavers. He enjoys roaming his woven lair each day, serving the serious buyers.⁠

An intelligent flying carpet named Cloud Cutter has hidden itself here among the other carpets. It is trying to evade his previous owner, a kholo assassin known as Spider.⁠
1964276272:
Stonehome

Stonehome is a temple dedicated to Gorum in Iron Harbor on the Island of Chakikoth. It was built and founded by the Gorumites who left Osprey Cove to found Iron Harbor.⁠ The building, composed of hewn stone and masonry, has two floors, a basement and a roof that is accessible by a ladder on the upper floor.⁠ It is protected by a gated wall within which exists both a stable and a well within the temple-keep's front courtyard.⁠ It also currently contains a secret tunnel to the Sky Metal Workshop of the ruin known as Rusthenge.⁠
1966710712:
Brinewall

Brinewall was an abandoned settlement and castle (see Brinewall Castle) built during the early part of the Chelaxian expansion into Varisia (see Everwar). Situated in northwestern Varisia where the Steam River flows into the Bunyip Bay,⁠ it was designed to encourage trade with, and fend off attacks from, raiders of the Lands of the Linnorm Kings.⁠ Recently, it gained a new lease of life as a port in the new kingdom of Eurythnia in New Thassilon.⁠
1968523372:
Path of Commencement

The Path of Commencement is a winding mountain path between Isger and Druma located southwest of Petitioner's Port⁠ and features exquisite dwarven stonemasonry, including the expertly carved stone bridge which resembles two dwarven kings reaching toward each other with hammers.⁠

Originally constructed during the empire of Tar Taargadth and nearly 4,000 years old, the Path of Commencement was named during its restoration, which was paid for by the Druman Kalistocrats in the aftermath of Aroden's death and in anticipation of Isgeri refugees coming to Druma via the path.⁠
1979456992:
Jula

Jula is a coastal village in the southern Sodden Lands, populated by hardy folk who defy the Eye of Abendego and refuse to leave the Sodden Lands for more temperate climes.⁠
1979831332:
Hall of Holies

The Hall of Holies is home to the Chamber of Ecclestials, the oldest district council in all Absalom and is even older than the Grand Council of Absalom. The Chamber of Ecclestials is made up of twenty members of prominent religions who meet within the hall once a month spending most of their time organizing and arranging holidays, festivals, celebrations, religious observances and protests between the near countless religions of the Ascendant Court, many of whom hate each other with a truly religious zeal. While keeping these seething cauldron of religious intrigue from boiling over is now a relatively mundane duty for the council they do sometimes meet in the event of a true crisis. Hall of Holies is a former temple of the dead god Aroden. In between meetings, the Hall of Holies is home to the bureaucrats and administrators who actually keep the Ascendant Court district running.⁠
1983797432:
Zhonar

Zhonar is a volcano located in the eastern Zho Mountains of Qadira. The eruptions of Zhonar and its companion Zhobl covered the nearby town of Shadun in ash and dust, forcing its inhabitants to abandon it.⁠
2010873962:
Laughing Gale

The Laughing Gale is one of many taverns in Greengold, though it stands out as the oldest and longest-running. It's a popular hangout, and many of the city's fights start after a drink here, sometimes spilling over into the rest of the city.⁠
2023605472:
Egede

The port city of Egede (pronounced eh-GEHD-eh)⁠ is located on the Lake of Mists and Veils. It is the second-largest city in the Mendev, and as the end of the River Road, is the first Mendevian city that most crusaders entered during the period of the Mendevian Crusades.⁠

From Egede, trade from neighbouring nations (in particular Brevoy, since the recent fall of House Rogarvia) usually flows into Mendev, as did crusaders traveling from the south through the River Kingdoms and Numeria. During the Mendevian Crusades, exhausted soldiers were often sent to Egede for much needed rest and relaxation, whether that was for prayer at the temples or a trip to the covert brothels and bawdy houses that thrived there. A great deal of work was also done here in support of the war effort, often by travelers thoroughly bankrupted by unscrupulous merchants on their way to the crusades.⁠

The growth of industry, trade, and business proved helpful to the crusaders' cause, but some have begun to worry that the city is becoming a den of sin and debauchery.
2031492342:
Pillars of Rovagug

The Pillars of Rovagug are a set of mountains in the far north of the World's Edge Mountains in Taldor.⁠⁠
2035773632:
Tourondel Marches

The Tourondel Marches surround the Tourondel River and mark the northern border of Nirmathas. The earliest settlements in the area date back to the Shining Crusade era, and several ruins can be found in the region, which is populated by orcs and undead who sometimes harass travelers. Those who reside in the area have developed skills as merchants and tend to have a more formal demeanor compared to their southern compatriots, likely based on their historical proximity to the lawful nation of Lastwall.⁠
2039167932:
Daigaki Castle

Daigaki Castle (pronounced dai-ga-kee)⁠ is a haunted stronghold in southern Linvarre in Tian Xia, and the lair of a large group of undead led by the ghost of Tsubokandu.

After the fall of Imperial Lung Wa in 7108 IC, the city of Kamikobu—now known as New Oppara—was besieged by a dozen bandit warlords and Tsubokandu was considered the cruelest of them all. Tsubokandu was a disgraced samurai warlord from the neighbouring kingdom of Songbai who chose exile over an honourable death.

Tsubokandu was defeated by the founder of Linvarre's predecessor colony of Amanandar, General Orphyrea Amanandar, but after his death his ghost returned to Daigaki Castle and began gathering an army of the dead to reap some unknown terrible revenge.⁠
2053609022:
Veka

Veka is an Iobarian town located on the shores of the Nyvyrd and has stood as a garrisoned fort since its founding. The easternmost Iobarian settlement in the Ice Steppes, it is home to a number of smithies, where all metal weapons and goods in the region are forged. The owner of these smithies is the ruthless Koffar Rjul, who holds control over the entire Nyvyrd region.⁠
